events.name: Asian Championships
story: China and Japan shared all seven titles in Tashkent, four to three. Tomokazu Harimoto came from two games down to beat Li Tianyang for the men's singles title, denying China a clean sweep of the men's events.

Chen Yi beat Miwa Harimoto 3-0 in the women's final, and Japan's women came from 2-1 down to beat China 3-2 in the team final, with Honoka Hashimoto winning the decider. Miwa Harimoto reached three finals and won the mixed doubles with Sora Matsushima.

China's men beat South Korea 3-0 in the team final. The Koreans, without Lim Jonghoon or Jang Woojin, had knocked out Japan 3-1 in the semi-finals. The championships also decided Asian qualifying places for the 2027 World Championships.

events.name: Americas Championships
story: Hugo Calderano and Adriana Diaz won the singles titles in Lima, where five countries won titles and none won more than two.

Calderano, the only player from the Americas in the men's world top 10, beat his Brazilian teammate Guilherme Teodoro 4-1 in the final. Diaz beat Canada's Mo Zhang 4-2 for her seventh continental singles title and her third in a row.

Zhang won the mixed doubles with Edward Ly, Chile's Nicolas Burgos and Gustavo Gomez the men's doubles, and Brazil's Giulia Takahashi and Laura Watanabe the women's doubles. The US women beat Puerto Rico 3-0 in the team final.

events.name: WTT Champions Doha
story: Lin Yun-Ju and Zhu Yuling won the first WTT Champions event of the year in Doha, in a week without Wang Chuqin or Sun Yingsha. Lin, outside the top eight seeds, beat South Korea's Jang Woojin 4-0 in the final, 11-7, 11-9, 11-9, 13-11.

His route was the harder part. Lin beat Sora Matsushima 4-0 in the quarter-finals and then came from two games down to beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-3 in the semi-finals. Jang, also unseeded, knocked out Truls Moregard and then the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-2. The biggest shock came in the first round, where Dimitrij Ovtcharov beat the second seed, Hugo Calderano, 3-2.

Zhu, the sixth seed, won the women's title for Macao by beating Chen Xingtong 4-2, taking the sixth game 13-11. She beat Wang Yidi in the quarter-finals and Germany's Han Ying in the semi-finals. Han had knocked out the top seed, Wang Manyu, 4-3 a round earlier.
Zhu stayed in Doha and won the Star Contender event the following week.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Doha
story: Zhu Yuling completed a Doha double a week after winning WTT Champions Doha, and Zhou Qihao won the men's title without being seeded. Zhu, the second seed, lost the first two games of the final to Japan's Hitomi Sato and then won four in a row, 11-7, 11-6, 11-6, 11-5.
Sato had the week of her career to that point. Unseeded, she beat the top seed, Kuai Man, 3-0 in the last 16 and reached the final without dropping a game in her quarter-final or semi-final.

The men's draw fell apart around Zhou. Ovtcharov beat the top seed, Lin Shidong, in the last 16, and China's Xue Fei knocked out the third seed, Tomokazu Harimoto. Zhou beat the fourth seed, Liang Jingkun, in the first round, then Ovtcharov 3-2 in the semi-finals and Wen Ruibo 4-2 in the final. Wen had beaten Hugo Calderano, the second seed, 3-2 in the semi-finals.

Japan's Sakura Yokoi and Satsuki Odo won the women's doubles, South Korea's Jang Woojin and Cho Daeseong beat Huang Youzheng and Wen 3-2 in the men's doubles, and Hong Kong's Wong Chun Ting and Doo Hoi Kem won the mixed.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Chennai
events.venue: Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University
story: The Czech Republic's Lubomir Jancarik won the biggest title of his career in Chennai, and Satsuki Odo won the women's event as top seed without dropping a game in the final.

Jancarik was unseeded and beat the fourth seed, India's Manav Thakkar, in the first round. He beat Sathiyan Gnanasekaran in the quarter-finals and South Korea's Park Ganghyeon 3-2 in the semi-finals, and then France's Thibault Poret 4-2 in the final. Poret had reached the final after a walkover from the top seed, Oh Junsung, and a 3-0 win over his teammate Flavien Coton. Ovtcharov, the second seed, lost to Park in the quarter-finals.
Odo beat Japan's Miu Hirano 4-0 in the final, 11-2, 11-7, 13-11, 11-5. Hirano had knocked out the second seed, Miyu Nagasaki, 3-2 in the last 16.

India's Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade reached the mixed doubles final in front of a home crowd and lost 3-0 to Romania's Eduard Ionescu and Bernadette Szőcs. Coton and Poret won the men's doubles after another walkover from Oh and Lim Jonghoon, and Japan's Sakura Yokoi and Sachi Aoki won the women's doubles.

events.name: Singapore Smash
story: Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha, the top seeds, won the first Grand Smash of the year. Sun beat Wang Manyu 4-2 in an all-Chinese women's final, winning the fifth game 12-10 and the sixth 11-9 after Wang had levelled at 2-2. It was her third Singapore Smash title.

Wang Chuqin beat Taiwan's Lin Yun-Ju 4-0 in the men's final, 11-3, 11-8, 11-8, 11-9, after a 4-1 win over Félix Lebrun in the semi-finals. Lebrun had knocked out the third seed, Lin Shidong, in the quarter-finals. Two of the top four seeds went out in the last 16: Hugo Calderano lost to China's Chen Yuanyu, and Tomokazu Harimoto to Germany's Patrick Franziska.
Germany's Sabine Winter was the surprise of the women's draw. Unseeded, she beat the fourth seed, Zhu Yuling, and the seventh, Wang Yidi, to reach the semi-finals, where she lost to Wang Manyu.

Félix and Alexis Lebrun won their first Grand Smash doubles title, beating Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng 3-0. Miwa Harimoto and Hina Hayata won the women's doubles, and Brazil's Hugo Calderano and Bruna Takahashi beat the top seeds, Lim Jonghoon and Shin Yubin, 3-0 for the mixed title.

events.name: WTT Champions Chongqing
story: Félix Lebrun and Miwa Harimoto won in Chongqing, where all four of the top women's seeds were out by the end of the quarter-finals and the men's top seed, Wang Chuqin, lost in the last eight.

Harimoto, the eighth seed, beat Kuai Man 4-3 in the final, winning the deciding game 11-5. Kuai had knocked out the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2 in the quarter-finals. Wang Manyu, the second seed, lost 3-0 to Japan's Satsuki Odo in the first round, and Chen Xingtong and Zhu Yuling also fell early.

Lebrun, the fifth seed, beat Hugo Calderano 4-3 in the quarter-finals and Sora Matsushima 4-3 in the semi-finals. Matsushima had beaten Wang Chuqin 4-2. In the final Lebrun beat China's Wen Ruibo 4-1, 11-5, 11-8, 9-11, 11-7, 13-11.

Wen, unseeded, had the run of the week. He beat the second seed, Truls Moregard, in the last 16, Germany's Dang Qiu in the quarter-finals and Tomokazu Harimoto 4-2 in the semi-finals, winning the sixth game 21-19.

events.name: World Cup Macao
story: Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha won the World Cup in Macao. The event opened with groups, and the winners went into a 16-player knockout draw.

Wang came closest to losing. Darko Jorgic led him 3-1 in the quarter-finals before Wang won the last three games, and in the final Japan's Sora Matsushima led 3-2. Wang took the last two games 11-4, 11-8 to win 4-3, after a second game he won 18-16. Matsushima, the seventh seed, had beaten Truls Moregard 4-0 and Lin Yun-Ju 4-3 on the way.

Sun beat Wang Manyu 4-1 in an all-Chinese women's final, 11-9, 11-8, 13-11, 8-11, 11-7. Her hardest match was in the quarter-finals, where Egypt's Hana Goda took her to 13-11 in the seventh game. Sabine Winter, unseeded, beat Wang Yidi 4-0 to reach the semi-finals, where Sun beat her by the same score.

events.name: World Team Championships
story: China won both team titles at the centenary World Championships in London, 100 years after the first world championships were held in the city. The group stage was played at the Copper Box Arena and OVO Arena Wembley, and the knockout rounds at Wembley.

China's men beat Japan 3-0 in the final for their 12th men's title in a row. Japan reached the final by beating Germany 3-1 and Chinese Taipei 3-0, while China beat South Korea 3-0 and France 3-1. Chinese Taipei and France took bronze.

The women's final was closer. China beat Japan 3-2, after Japan had beaten Ukraine and Germany 3-0. China beat South Korea and Romania without losing a match. Romania, who beat France 3-1 in the quarter-finals, and Germany took bronze.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Ljubljana
story: Japan won four of the five titles in Ljubljana. Shunsuke Togami, unseeded, won the men's singles and doubles, and Hina Hayata won the women's singles and doubles.

The top two men's seeds went out early: Félix Lebrun lost to Hiroto Shinozuka in the last 16, and Lin Shidong to Yukiya Uda in the first round. Togami beat Germany's Dang Qiu 3-2 in the semi-finals and then Hugo Calderano 4-3 in the final, winning the seventh game 11-7.
Hayata, the eighth seed, beat her doubles partner and the top seed, Miwa Harimoto, 3-0 in the semi-finals. In the final she beat Macao's Zhu Yuling 4-3, 11-9 in the seventh game.

Togami and Shinozuka beat Wen Ruibo and Huang Youzheng 3-2 for the men's doubles, Harimoto and Hayata beat their teammates Satsuki Odo and Sakura Yokoi for the women's, and South Korea's Lim Jonghoon and Shin Yubin beat Germany's Dang Qiu and Sabine Winter in the mixed.

events.name: United States Smash
story: Sora Matsushima won the United States Smash, held at the Ontario Convention Center outside Los Angeles, and Sun Yingsha won the women's event.

The men's top two seeds went out in the last 16. Denmark's Anders Lind beat Wang Chuqin 3-1, and Vladimir Sidorenko, a neutral athlete, beat Tomokazu Harimoto 3-0. Sidorenko then beat the third seed, Truls Moregard, 4-3 in the semi-finals. Matsushima, the sixth seed, beat Félix Lebrun 4-1 and then Sidorenko 4-2 in the final.

Sun beat Kuai Man 4-3 in the women's final, winning the seventh game 11-4 after Kuai had come back from 3-1 down. The second seed, Wang Manyu, lost 3-0 to Japan's Hitomi Sato in the first round, and Kuai beat Miwa Harimoto 4-3 in the semi-finals.

Wang Manyu and Kuai won the women's doubles, Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen beat the top seeds, Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng, 3-2 in the men's, and Lim Jonghoon and Shin Yubin beat Wang Chuqin and Sun 3-2 in the mixed.

events.name: WTT Star Contender São José dos Campos
story: Hugo Calderano won at home in Brazil, beating Alexis Lebrun 4-3 in the final with an 11-9 seventh game. The top seed needed five games in the semi-finals against Japan's Yukiya Uda, where he won the fourth game 21-19 to level the match.
Hina Hayata won the women's singles as top seed, beating her compatriot Hitomi Sato 4-2 in the final, and added the women's doubles with Kaho Akae.

Calderano and Bruna Takahashi, the top seeds, lost the mixed doubles final 3-1 to Japan's Shunsuke Togami and Satsuki Odo. Hong Kong's Wong Chun Ting and Chan Baldwin won the men's doubles, beating France's Joe Seyfried and Vincent Picard 3-2.

events.name: WTT Champions Yokohama
story: Tomokazu and Miwa Harimoto, brother and sister, won both titles at Japan's home Champions event.
Miwa, the top seed, beat Chen Xingtong 4-2 in the final, 13-11, 11-7, 9-11, 11-9, 1-11, 11-7, after a 4-2 win over Wang Yidi in the semi-finals.

Tomokazu, the third seed, beat the top seed and his teammate Sora Matsushima 4-2 in the semi-finals. In the final he beat South Korea's Oh Junsung 4-1. Oh, unseeded, had beaten Hiroto Shinozuka 4-1 in the other semi-final. Lim Jonghoon knocked out the fourth seed, Lin Yun-Ju, in the first round.

events.name: Europe Smash
story: Félix Lebrun and Wang Manyu won the Europe Smash in Malmö, and the Lebrun brothers added the men's doubles.

Sweden's Truls Moregard, the top seed, lost his first match at home, 3-0 to Germany's Dimitrij Ovtcharov. Lebrun, the third seed, beat Darko Jorgic 4-0 in the semi-finals and Tomokazu Harimoto 4-1 in the final, 11-5, 11-8, 5-11, 11-9, 11-9. Harimoto had beaten Sora Matsushima 4-3 in the other semi-final.
Wang Manyu, the top seed, beat her teammate Wang Yidi 4-2 in the women's final. Wang Yidi had knocked out the second seed, Miwa Harimoto, 4-2 in the semi-finals.
Félix and Alexis Lebrun beat Hong Kong's Wong Chun Ting and Chan Baldwin 3-0 in the men's doubles final. Miwa Harimoto and Hina Hayata won the women's doubles, and Lin Shidong and Kuai Man the mixed.

events.name: WTT Champions Macao
story: Truls Moregard and Miwa Harimoto won WTT Champions Macao. Moregard, the third seed, beat Hugo Calderano 4-1 in the final after saving his semi-final against Tomokazu Harimoto, which he won 16-14 in the seventh game.
Miwa Harimoto, the top seed, led China's Chen Yi 2-0 in the final, trailed 3-2 and won the last two games, the seventh 12-10. Chen, the eighth seed, had beaten Hina Hayata 4-3 in the semi-finals.

Two of the top three women's seeds lost their first match. Egypt's Dina Meshref beat the third seed, Wang Yidi, 3-1, and Germany's Han Ying beat the second seed, Kuai Man, 3-2. France's Flavien Coton knocked out the men's fourth seed, Lin Yun-Ju.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Astana
story: Japan's Miyuu Kihara won the women's singles in Astana without being seeded, and Germany's Dang Qiu beat the top seed, Alexis Lebrun, in the men's final.

Kihara beat the second seed, Satsuki Odo, 3-2 in the semi-finals and Hitomi Sato 4-3 in the final, 11-8 in the seventh game. She also won the women's doubles with Miu Hirano and reached the mixed doubles final with Hiromu Kobayashi.

Dang, the second seed, lost the first game of the final and then won four of the next five against Lebrun, 4-2. China's Li Tianyang, unseeded, knocked out the third seed, Darko Jorgic, and reached the semi-finals.
Romania's Eduard Ionescu and Darius Movileanu won the men's doubles, and China's Chen Junsong and Wang Yidi the mixed.

events.name: China Smash
story: Sora Matsushima and Wang Manyu won the China Smash in Beijing, which started without Wang Chuqin and Lin Shidong. Both men withdrew injured two days after the Asian Games men's singles final.

Matsushima, the second seed, led Taiwan's Lin Yun-Ju 2-0 in the final, trailed 3-2 and won the last two games, the seventh 11-9. Lin had beaten Hugo Calderano 4-3 in the semi-finals, and China's Zhou Qihao knocked out the third seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, 3-0 in the last 16.

Sun Yingsha, the second seed, lost her first match, 3-1 to Thailand's Orawan Paranang. Wang Manyu, the top seed, beat Japan's Hitomi Sato 4-0 in the final. Sato, unseeded, had beaten Chen Xingtong 4-1 in the semi-finals.

Wang Manyu and Kuai Man won the women's doubles against Miwa Harimoto and Hina Hayata. South Korea's Lim Jonghoon won two titles: the men's doubles with Oh Junsung, beating the Lebrun brothers 3-1, and the mixed with Shin Yubin.

events.name: Asian Games
story: Japan's men ended China's 32-year hold on the Asian Games team title, and Lin Shidong won three gold medals at Sky Hall Toyota.

Japan beat China 3-2 in the men's team final. Wang Chuqin beat Sora Matsushima in the opening match and Tomokazu Harimoto beat Wang 3-0 to level at 2-2, before Matsushima beat Wen Ruibo 3-2 in the decider. China had won the event at every Games since 1994.

Lin won the mixed doubles with Kuai Man, beating Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha 4-0, the men's doubles with Huang Youzheng against Harimoto and Hiroto Shinozuka, and the men's singles against Wang Chuqin on the last day. Two days later both Lin and Wang withdrew injured from the China Smash.

Wang Manyu won the women's singles, beating Sun 4-2 and taking the sixth game 15-13, eight years after her first Asian Games singles title in 2018. She also won the women's doubles with Kuai, and China beat Japan 3-0 in the women's team final.

events.name: European Championships
story: Félix Lebrun won the European men's singles title in Ljubljana, two years after his brother Alexis won it in Linz, and Elizabet Abraamian became the first qualifier to win the women's title.

Lebrun, the top seed, trailed Sweden's Anton Källberg 3-2 in the final and won the last two games 11-6, 11-1. "I played the best game of my life in the last one," he told the ETTU. A day earlier the Lebrun brothers had kept their men's doubles title, beating Källberg and Kristian Karlsson 3-2. France's Léo de Nodrest, seeded 67th, became the first men's qualifier to reach the semi-finals since qualification groups began in 2012.

Abraamian, seeded 35th, beat Germany's Annett Kaufmann 4-3 in the last match of the championships. Kaufmann led 10-8 in the fifth game, but Abraamian won it 12-10 and took the seventh 11-6. Both had already played a seven-game semi-final that day. France's Prithika Pavade, who knocked out the top seed, Sabine Winter, took bronze with Nina Mittelham.
Germany's Benedikt Duda and Mittelham won the mixed doubles, and Slovakia's Tatiana Kukulkova and Poland's Natalia Bajor the women's doubles. France topped the medal table with six medals.

events.name: African Championships

champions.note: Egypt's third individual title of the week
Goda's second title of the week
Abdelaziz's third title of the week

story: Egypt won every individual title at the African Championships in Tangier. Youssef Abdelaziz beat his teammate Omar Assar 4-1 in the men's singles final and also won the men's and mixed doubles.
Hana Goda, 18, won her fourth African women's singles title in a row, beating Dina Meshref 4-1, and the pair also won the women's doubles. Egypt took all four medals in the women's singles.
Egypt's women won the team event without losing a match in the final, beating Tunisia 3-0.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Doha
story: Tomokazu Harimoto and Kuai Man won the first WTT Star Contender event of the year in Doha. Harimoto, the top seed, beat Denmark's Jonathan Groth 4-0 in the final, 11-9, 13-11, 11-9, 11-6, after a 3-0 semi-final win over Quadri Aruna. Kuai, who was unseeded, beat Japan's Miyuu Kihara 4-0, 11-6, 11-3, 11-8, 11-3.

The women's draw lost its top two seeds early. Miwa Harimoto, the second seed, went out to Thailand's Orawan Paranang in the last 32, and Chen Yi beat the top seed, Hina Hayata, 3-2 in the last 16. Groth's run to the final included a 3-2 quarter-final win over the second seed, Dang Qiu, taken 12-10 in the fifth game.

events.name: Singapore Smash
story: Sun Yingsha and Lin Shidong won the singles titles at the Singapore Smash. Sun, the top seed, beat Kuai Man 4-1 in the final, 11-8, 9-11, 11-7, 11-5, 11-6. Lin, the second seed, beat Liang Jingkun 4-2 in the men's final, 9-11, 11-8, 11-8, 6-11, 11-3, 11-2, winning the last two games for the loss of five points.

Liang had knocked out the top seed, Wang Chuqin, 4-3 in the semi-finals, winning the seventh game 12-10. Lin left Singapore with three titles, adding the men's doubles with Wang and the mixed doubles with Kuai, who also won the women's doubles with Wang Manyu after beating her 3-0 in the singles last 16.

events.name: WTT Champions Chongqing
events.venue: Huaxi LIVE-Yudong Sports and Culture Center
story: Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha won WTT Champions Chongqing. Wang, the second seed, beat the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-1 in the final, 11-5, 6-11, 11-7, 11-5, 11-6. Sun, the women's top seed, beat Chen Xingtong 4-0, 11-7, 11-4, 12-10, 11-7.

Sun's hardest match came in the semi-finals, where she lost the first two games to Wang Yidi and then won four in a row. Chen beat the second seed, Wang Manyu, 4-2 in the other semi-final. Tomokazu Harimoto was the only player from outside China to reach the last four, losing 4-1 to Wang Chuqin.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Chennai
story: South Korea's Oh Junsung and Japan's Miwa Harimoto won WTT Star Contender Chennai. Oh, who was unseeded, came from 3-2 down to beat France's Thibault Poret 4-3 in the final, 9-11, 11-7, 11-3, 9-11, 6-11, 11-4, 11-7. Harimoto, the second seed, beat her compatriot Honoka Hashimoto 4-2.

Both men's top seeds went out in the last 16: Tomokazu Harimoto lost 3-1 to Croatia's Tomislav Pucar and Hugo Calderano 3-2 to Lim Jonghoon. Hashimoto beat the women's top seed, Hina Hayata, 3-2 on her way to the final. Lim won two titles, the men's doubles with An Jaehyun and the mixed doubles with Shin Yubin.

events.name: WTT Champions Incheon
story: Xiang Peng and Wang Yidi won WTT Champions Incheon. Xiang, who was unseeded, beat the home player Lee Sang Su 4-0 in the final, 11-8, 11-0, 11-3, 11-4. Wang, the top seed, came from 3-1 down to beat Chen Xingtong 4-3, winning the seventh game 12-10.

Xiang knocked out the second seed, Hugo Calderano, 4-1 in the quarter-finals and Patrick Franziska 4-2 in the semi-finals. Lee beat the sixth seed, Lin Gaoyuan, and then Lin Yun-Ju, who had knocked out the top seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, 3-1 in the last 16.

events.name: World Cup Macao
story: Hugo Calderano won the World Cup in Macao, the first player from the Americas to do so. The Brazilian, seeded fifth, lost the first game of the final to the top seed, Lin Shidong, and then won four in a row, 6-11, 11-7, 11-9, 11-4, 11-5. Sun Yingsha beat Kuai Man 4-0 in the women's final, 11-9, 11-6, 11-9, 11-6.

Calderano beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-1 in the quarter-finals and then the second seed, Wang Chuqin, 4-3 in the semi-finals, taking the seventh game 12-10. Kuai came from two games down to beat the second seed, Wang Manyu, in the quarter-finals and from 2-0 down again to beat Mima Ito 4-3 in the semi-finals.

events.name: World Championships
story: Wang Chuqin won his first world singles title in Doha, beating Hugo Calderano 4-1 in the final, 12-10, 11-3, 4-11, 11-2, 11-7. Sun Yingsha kept the women's title, beating Wang Manyu 4-3 in a final that went the distance, 11-6, 12-10, 8-11, 5-11, 12-10, 11-13, 11-7.

Calderano became the first player from the Americas to reach a world final. He beat Liang Jingkun 4-3 in the semi-finals after Liang had knocked out the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-3 in the quarter-finals. China won four of the five titles: Wang Manyu and Kuai Man took the women's doubles and Wang Chuqin and Sun the mixed, while Japan's Hiroto Shinozuka and Shunsuke Togami beat Taiwan's Kao Cheng-Jui and Lin Yun-Ju 3-2 in the men's doubles final.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Ljubljana
story: Hugo Calderano and Miyu Nagasaki won WTT Star Contender Ljubljana. Calderano, the top seed, beat Félix Lebrun 4-2 in the final, 12-10, 15-13, 11-13, 8-11, 11-9, 11-6, a day after coming from two games down to beat Alexis Lebrun in the semi-finals. Nagasaki, who was unseeded, beat her compatriot Miyuu Kihara 4-1.

The women's top three seeds were all gone before the semi-finals. Chen Yi beat the top seed, Miwa Harimoto, 3-2, Zhu Yuling beat the second seed, Satsuki Odo, 3-2, and Kihara had beaten the third seed, Hina Hayata, 3-0 in the last 16. South Korea won the men's doubles and the mixed doubles.

events.name: United States Smash
story: Wang Chuqin and Zhu Yuling won the United States Smash in Las Vegas. Wang, the second seed, beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-0 in the final, 11-3, 11-6, 12-10, 11-8. Zhu, who was unseeded, came from two games down to beat Chen Yi 4-2, 7-11, 8-11, 11-7, 11-5, 11-9, 11-8.

The women's draw lost three of its top four seeds in the last 16: Chen Yi beat the top seed, Sun Yingsha, Zhu beat the second seed, Wang Manyu, and Honoka Hashimoto beat Wang Yidi. Harimoto came from 3-2 down to beat the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-3 in the semi-finals, and Wang beat Félix Lebrun 4-3 in the other.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Foz do Iguaçu
story: Hugo Calderano won at home in Foz do Iguaçu, beating Germany's Benedikt Duda 4-3 in the final, 11-7, 11-7, 9-11, 11-8, 9-11, 10-12, 11-8. Calderano, the top seed, led 3-1 before Duda drew level. Miwa Harimoto, the women's top seed, beat Miyu Nagasaki 4-2.

All four women's semi-finalists were Japanese, and Nagasaki beat the second seed, Satsuki Odo, 3-0 to reach the final. Duda beat his compatriot Dimitrij Ovtcharov 3-0 in the semi-finals, and then won the men's doubles with Dang Qiu.

events.name: WTT Champions Yokohama
story: Tomokazu Harimoto won WTT Champions Yokohama in front of a home crowd, beating Wang Chuqin 4-2 in the final, 11-9, 11-5, 11-8, 9-11, 11-13, 11-4. Chen Xingtong beat the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2 in the women's final, 6-11, 11-8, 11-3, 11-5, 6-11, 11-5.

The top seed, Lin Shidong, lost 3-2 to Dang Qiu in the last 16. Kanak Jha of the US beat Dang in the quarter-finals to reach the last four, where Harimoto beat him 4-1. In the women's draw Chen Yi knocked out the second seed, Wang Manyu, 3-2 in the last 16.

events.name: Europe Smash
story: Truls Moregard won the Europe Smash at home in Malmö, beating the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-3 in the final, 11-8, 8-11, 12-10, 11-8, 4-11, 11-13, 11-9. Sun Yingsha beat Wang Manyu 4-2 for the women's title, 11-9, 11-9, 5-11, 10-12, 11-6, 11-5.

Moregard, the sixth seed, led 3-1 before Lin drew level, and he had beaten Benedikt Duda 4-0 in the semi-finals. Duda had knocked out the second seed, Hugo Calderano, 4-0, and Liang Jingkun and Tomokazu Harimoto both lost before the quarter-finals. Sun and Wang won the women's doubles together.

events.name: WTT Champions Macao
story: Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha won WTT Champions Macao. Wang beat Hugo Calderano 4-0 in the final, 11-9, 11-7, 11-9, 11-4, without dropping a game in the semi-final or final. Sun came from 3-2 down to beat Wang Manyu 4-3, 11-8, 13-15, 11-9, 9-11, 5-11, 11-9, 11-6.
Denmark's Anders Lind knocked out the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-3 in the quarter-finals before losing 4-0 to Calderano. The third seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, lost to Xue Fei in the first round.

events.name: China Smash
story: Wang Chuqin and Wang Manyu won the China Smash in Beijing. Wang Chuqin, the top seed, beat Félix Lebrun 4-0 in the final, 11-7, 11-2, 11-5, 11-7. Wang Manyu beat the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2, 10-12, 11-7, 11-9, 11-5, 8-11, 11-2.

Wang Chuqin came from 3-1 down to beat Xiang Peng 4-3 in the semi-finals and left with three titles, adding the men's doubles with Lin Shidong and the mixed doubles with Sun. Lebrun beat Lin 4-2 in the other semi-final. Wang Manyu also won the women's doubles with Kuai Man.

events.name: WTT Star Contender London
story: Dang Qiu and Miwa Harimoto won WTT Star Contender London. Dang, the fourth seed, won the first three games of the final against the top seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, and beat him 4-2, 13-11, 12-10, 14-12, 9-11, 7-11, 12-10. Miwa Harimoto came from two games down to beat Hina Hayata 4-3.

Poland's Milosz Redzimski reached the semi-finals, where he lost 3-2 to Dang, and Sweden's Kristian Karlsson knocked out the second seed, Darko Jorgic, in the last 32. Singapore's Zeng Jian beat the women's second seed, Mima Ito, 3-2. Taiwan won the men's doubles and the mixed doubles.

events.name: WTT Champions Montpellier
story: Truls Moregard and Wang Yidi won WTT Champions Montpellier. Moregard, the fourth seed, beat Sora Matsushima 4-0 in the final, 11-9, 11-8, 11-7, 11-9. Wang came from two games down to beat Germany's Sabine Winter 4-3, 8-11, 10-12, 11-5, 11-4, 6-11, 12-10, 11-9.

The men's top three seeds went out early. Kanak Jha beat Hugo Calderano in the first round, and Tomokazu Harimoto and Félix Lebrun lost to Alexis Lebrun and Simon Gauzy in the last 16. In the women's draw the first, second and fourth seeds, Chen Xingtong, Kuai Man and Zhu Yuling, all lost their first matches. Winter, who was unseeded, came from 3-0 down to beat Doo Hoi Kem in the quarter-finals.

events.name: WTT Champions Frankfurt
story: Sora Matsushima and Hina Hayata won WTT Champions Frankfurt. Matsushima, who was unseeded and had lost the Montpellier final a week earlier, beat Dang Qiu 4-1, 11-8, 15-13, 11-13, 18-16, 11-9. Hayata beat the top seed, Miwa Harimoto, 4-3 in an all-Japanese women's final, 11-4, 11-8, 4-11, 6-11, 11-6, 9-11, 11-9.

The men's top three seeds were gone before the quarter-finals: Anton Källberg beat Truls Moregard 3-0, Simon Gauzy beat Hugo Calderano and Dimitrij Ovtcharov beat Tomokazu Harimoto. Japan had three of the four women's semi-finalists, and there was no Chinese player in the quarter-finals.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Muscat
story: Félix Lebrun beat his brother Alexis 4-3 in the final of WTT Star Contender Muscat, 11-8, 11-8, 11-4, 5-11, 13-15, 10-12, 11-6, after Félix had won the first three games and Alexis the next three. Miyuu Kihara beat South Korea's Joo Cheonhui 4-1 in the women's final.

France had three of the four men's semi-finalists, with Flavien Coton losing 3-2 to Alexis. Kihara, the seventh seed, beat the second seed, Satsuki Odo, 3-0 in the semi-finals after the top seed, Hina Hayata, lost to Lee Eunhye in the last 16.

events.name: WTT Finals Hong Kong
story: Tomokazu Harimoto and Wang Manyu won the WTT Finals in Hong Kong. Harimoto beat Truls Moregard 4-2 in the final, 11-8, 5-11, 11-9, 10-12, 14-12, 11-2, after beating Lin Shidong 4-3 in the semi-finals. Wang beat Kuai Man 4-2, 11-7, 8-11, 11-8, 11-8, 9-11, 12-10.

Moregard reached the final without playing his semi-final when the top seed, Wang Chuqin, withdrew. Kuai beat the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2 in the women's semi-finals. South Korea's Lim Jonghoon and Shin Yubin beat Wang Chuqin and Sun 3-0 in the mixed doubles final.

events.name: Asian Championships
story: China won both team titles at the Asian Championships in Bhubaneswar, which had no individual events this time. The men beat Hong Kong 3-0 in the final and the women beat Japan 3-0, with Wang Manyu, Sun Yingsha and Kuai Man each winning a match.

The men's semi-final was much closer. Japan led China 2-0 after Tomokazu Harimoto beat Liang Jingkun and Sora Matsushima beat Wang Chuqin, before Lin Shidong, Wang and Liang won the last three matches. The women's title came back to China a year after Japan had won it.

events.name: European Team Championships
story: France won the men's title at the European Team Championships in Zadar for the first time since 1998, beating Romania 3-0 in the final with wins for Alexis Lebrun, Félix Lebrun and Simon Gauzy. Germany beat Romania 3-0 in the women's final for their 10th title and their third in a row.

Romania's men were in their first final. France had ended Germany's run of 12 men's finals in a row in the semi-finals. In the women's final Annett Kaufmann beat Bernadette Szőcs 3-2, having not won a game against her in their two earlier meetings, and Germany's women did not lose a match all week.

events.name: Pan American Championships
story: Hugo Calderano and Adriana Díaz won the singles titles at the Pan American Championships in Rock Hill, the first held in the US. Calderano beat Kanak Jha 4-1 in the final, and Díaz beat the top seed, Bruna Takahashi, 4-0 after winning every match of the tournament 4-0. Calderano also won the mixed doubles with Takahashi.

The hosts reached both team finals and lost both. Argentina beat the US 3-2 in the men's final despite two wins for Jha, and Puerto Rico, who had beaten the top seeds, Brazil, in the semi-finals, beat the US 3-1 for the women's title. Guatemala's Lucía Cordero and Hidalynn Zapata won the women's doubles.

events.name: African Championships
story: Egypt won all seven titles at the African Championships in Tunis. Omar Assar came from 3-1 down to beat Youssef Abdelaziz 4-3 in the men's final, winning the sixth game 16-14, for a record fifth African singles title. Hana Goda beat Dina Meshref 4-0 for her third women's title in a row.

Abdelaziz won two doubles titles, the men's with Mohamed El-Beiali and the mixed with Mariam Alhodaby. Egypt beat Algeria in the men's team final and Uganda 3-0 in the women's, Uganda having become the first East African side to reach that final.

events.name: Oceania Championships
story: Australia won all seven titles at the Oceania Championships in Christchurch. Nicholas Lum beat his teammate Aditya Sareen 4-2 in the men's final, 12-10, 6-11, 11-7, 7-11, 11-8, 12-10, and Yangzi Liu won the women's singles.

Lum won three titles, adding the men's doubles with Finn Luu and the mixed doubles with Liu, who also won the women's doubles with Minhyung Jee. Australia's men's and women's teams completed the sweep.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Doha
story: Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha won the singles at WTT Star Contender Doha. Wang, the second seed, beat Lin Shidong 4-2 in the final, 11-8, 11-3, 10-12, 11-7, 4-11, 11-5. Sun, the top seed, beat Chen Meng 4-1, taking the fifth game 12-10.

Lin had beaten the top seed, Fan Zhendong, in the quarter-finals, winning the deciding game 11-0, and Lin Gaoyuan knocked out Ma Long at the same stage. Sun and Wang won the mixed doubles, beating Lin Shidong and Kuai Man in five games, but Wang lost the men's doubles final with Ma to Liang Jingkun and Yuan Licen.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Goa
story: Félix Lebrun and Cheng I-Ching won the singles at WTT Star Contender Goa. Lebrun, the second seed, lost the first two games of the final against the top seed, Hugo Calderano, then won four in a row, 9-11, 9-11, 13-11, 11-0, 15-13, 11-7. Cheng beat Nina Mittelham 4-0, taking the third game 17-15.

Mittelham had knocked out the women's top seed, Shin Yubin, 3-2 in the semi-finals. South Korea won all three doubles titles: Shin and Jeon Jihee the women's, Lim Jonghoon and An Jaehyun the men's, and Shin and Lim the mixed.

events.name: World Team Championships
story: China won both titles at the World Team Championships in Busan. The men beat France 3-0 in the final, with wins for Wang Chuqin, Fan Zhendong and Ma Long. The women beat Japan 3-2 after trailing 2-1, when Hina Hayata beat Chen Meng and Miu Hirano beat Wang Yidi; Sun Yingsha and Chen then won the last two matches.

China's men came closest to losing in the semi-finals, where South Korea led 2-1 after Jang Woojin beat Wang and Lee Sang Su beat Ma 3-2. Fan and Wang won the last two matches. France reached the final by beating Chinese Taipei 3-1, and Chinese Taipei had knocked out the second seeds, Germany, 3-0 in the quarter-finals.

events.name: Singapore Smash
story: Wang Chuqin and Wang Manyu won the singles titles at the Singapore Smash. Wang Chuqin, the second seed, beat Liang Jingkun 4-1 in the final, and Wang Manyu, the third seed, beat Wang Yidi 4-1, 11-8, 11-5, 11-4, 7-11, 11-1.

The men's draw lost its top seed early. Lin Shidong beat Fan Zhendong 3-1 in the last 32, Patrick Franziska beat Ma Long in five games and Timo Boll took Liang to seven games in the quarter-finals. In the women's draw Chen Xingtong beat the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2 in the quarter-finals. Ma and Lin Gaoyuan won the men's doubles, beating Fan and Wang Chuqin 14-12 in the fifth game.

events.name: WTT Champions Incheon
story: Liang Jingkun and Sun Yingsha won WTT Champions Incheon. Liang, the second seed, beat Hugo Calderano 4-1 in the final, 11-6, 6-11, 11-8, 11-7, 11-5, a day after coming through 4-3 against Ma Long. Sun, the top seed, beat Wang Manyu 4-0 without conceding more than seven points in a game.

Calderano, seeded sixth, beat Félix Lebrun 3-0 in the quarter-finals and the top seed, Fan Zhendong, 4-2 in the semi-finals. Liang had saved his tournament in the quarter-finals, coming from two games down to beat Simon Gauzy 3-2.

events.name: World Cup Macao
story: Ma Long and Sun Yingsha won the World Cup in Macao, both from behind in seven-game finals. Ma lost the first three games against Lin Gaoyuan, then won four in a row, 11-8, 11-6, 11-4, 11-8. Sun trailed Wang Manyu 3-1 in games and won the last three.

Ma had beaten the top seed, Wang Chuqin, 4-0 in the semi-finals, and Lin Gaoyuan knocked out the second seed, Fan Zhendong, in the quarter-finals. Miwa Harimoto beat the third seed, Wang Yidi, in the women's last 16 and reached the semi-finals, where she lost 4-2 to Wang Manyu.

events.name: Saudi Smash
story: Wang Chuqin and Chen Meng won the singles at the first Saudi Smash in Jeddah. Wang, the top seed, beat Patrick Franziska 4-2 in the final, 11-2, 11-7, 11-5, 8-11, 10-12, 11-6. Chen, the fourth seed, beat the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2.

Franziska was unseeded. He beat the second seed, Fan Zhendong, 3-2 in the last 16 after losing the first two games, then Dang Qiu and Jang Woojin, who had knocked out Ma Long in the last 32. Manika Batra beat the women's second seed, Wang Manyu, in the last 32. China won all three doubles titles, with Wang Chuqin taking the men's with Ma and the mixed with Sun.

events.name: WTT Champions Chongqing
story: Fan Zhendong and Sun Yingsha won WTT Champions Chongqing, both in seven games. Fan, the third seed, led the top seed, Wang Chuqin, 3-0 in the final, lost the next three games and won the seventh 11-4. Sun beat Wang Manyu 4-3, taking the deciding game 11-9.

Hugo Calderano knocked out the second seed, Liang Jingkun, 3-2 in the quarter-finals before losing 4-0 to Fan. Dang Qiu came from two games down to beat Félix Lebrun and took two games off Wang in the semi-finals.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Ljubljana
story: Hugo Calderano and Hina Hayata won WTT Star Contender Ljubljana. Calderano, the second seed, beat the top seed, Félix Lebrun, 4-0 in the final, 11-9, 11-5, 11-7, 11-9. Hayata, the women's top seed, beat Prithika Pavade 4-0.

Pavade, who was unseeded, beat Mima Ito, Miu Hirano and the second seed, Shin Yubin, on her way to the final, taking the third game against Shin 20-18. Hayata and Tomokazu Harimoto won the mixed doubles, and Sweden's Anton Källberg and Kristian Karlsson the men's doubles.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Bangkok
story: Tomokazu Harimoto and Mima Ito won WTT Star Contender Bangkok. Harimoto, the third seed, beat the top seed, Lin Gaoyuan, 4-0 in the final, 11-3, 11-8, 11-6, 11-9. Ito beat her compatriot Honoka Hashimoto 4-2.

Hashimoto, who was unseeded, knocked out the second seed, Miwa Harimoto, in the last 32 and Shin Yubin in the semi-finals, and Suh Hyo Won beat the top seed, Chen Xingtong, in the last 16. Harimoto won three titles, adding the men's doubles with Sora Matsushima and the mixed doubles with Hina Hayata.

events.name: Olympic Games
story: China won all five table tennis gold medals at Paris 2024. Fan Zhendong beat Truls Moregard 4-1 in the men's singles final, Chen Meng retained her title by beating Sun Yingsha 4-2, and Wang Chuqin and Sun beat North Korea's Ri Jong Sik and Kim Kum Yong 4-2 in the mixed doubles. The men beat Sweden 3-0 and the women beat Japan 3-0 in the team finals.

Moregard, who was unseeded, knocked out the world No 1, Wang, 4-2 in the last 32 and beat Hugo Calderano in the semi-finals. Fan came from two games down to beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-3 in the quarter-finals. Sweden's men also beat the second seeds, Germany, 3-0 and came from 2-0 down to beat Japan in the semi-finals.

events.name: WTT Champions Macao
story: Lin Shidong and Sun Yingsha won WTT Champions Macao. Lin, who was unseeded, beat Dang Qiu 4-0 in the final, 11-5, 11-6, 11-8, 11-8. Sun, the top seed, beat Wang Yidi 4-2.

Lin beat the fourth seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, in the last 16 and the top seed, Wang Chuqin, 4-1 in the semi-finals. Dang, the eighth seed, came from two games down to beat the second seed, Liang Jingkun, in the quarter-finals. Wang Yidi beat Wang Manyu 4-0 in the women's semi-finals.

events.name: China Smash
story: Lin Shidong and Sun Yingsha won the singles at the China Smash in Beijing. Lin, the sixth seed, beat Ma Long 4-3 in the final after trailing 3-1, winning the last three games 11-4, 11-5, 11-8. Sun, the top seed, beat Wang Manyu 4-2.

Anders Lind beat the top seed, Wang Chuqin, 3-1 in the last 32 and reached the quarter-finals, and Xiang Peng beat Félix Lebrun and Truls Moregard. Ma, the fifth seed, beat Hugo Calderano and Liang Jingkun without dropping a game. Lin also won the mixed doubles with Kuai Man but lost the men's doubles final with Lin Gaoyuan to Wang and Liang.

events.name: Asian Championships

runner_up.name: Ri Jong Sik / Kim Kum Yong

story: Japan beat China 3-1 in the women's team final at the Asian Championships in Astana, Japan's first Asian women's team title with China in the field since 1974. Miwa Harimoto beat Wang Yidi and then Sun Yingsha, coming from two games down against Sun. China's men beat Chinese Taipei 3-1 for their title.

No Chinese player won a singles title. Tomokazu Harimoto beat Lin Shidong 3-1 in the men's final, after Oh Junsung had knocked out Wang Chuqin in the quarter-finals. North Korea's Kim Kum Yong beat Miwa Harimoto 3-1 in the women's final, and no Chinese woman reached the semi-finals: Sun withdrew from the singles after the team event with an arm problem.

events.name: European Championships
story: Alexis Lebrun and Sofia Polcanova won the singles at the European Championships in Linz. Lebrun beat Benedikt Duda 4-0 in the final, 11-5, 11-8, 11-6, 11-2, and Polcanova, playing at home, beat Bernadette Szőcs 4-1 to keep the title she won in Munich in 2022.

Lebrun beat Truls Moregard 4-0 in the semi-finals and also won the men's doubles with his brother Félix. Duda beat Dimitrij Ovtcharov in six games in the other semi-final. Polcanova lost two finals: the women's doubles with Szőcs, to Hana Matelová and Barbora Balážová, and the mixed doubles with Robert Gardos, to Álvaro Robles and María Xiao.

events.name: Pan American Championships
story: Hugo Calderano and Adriana Díaz won the singles at the Pan American Championships in San Salvador. Calderano beat his Brazil teammate Vitor Ishiy 4-0 in the final, 11-5, 11-7, 11-8, 11-9, and Díaz beat Bruna Takahashi for her fifth Pan American singles title.

Calderano and Takahashi lost the mixed doubles final 3-2 to Guilherme Teodoro and Takahashi's sister Giulia, who also won the women's doubles with Laura Watanabe. The United States beat Argentina 3-0 in the men's team final, after Argentina had knocked out the top seeds, Brazil, and Cuba beat Chile 3-1 for the women's team title.

events.name: African Championships
story: Egypt won five of the seven titles at the African Championships in Addis Ababa. Omar Assar beat Youssef Abdel-Aziz 4-2 in the men's singles final, and Hana Goda beat Mariam Alhodaby 4-3, 11-8 in the seventh game. Egypt's women beat Nigeria 3-0 in the team final.

Nigeria's men won the team title for the first time since 2018, beating Algeria 3-1 with two wins for Quadri Aruna. Aruna then withdrew from the singles with a thigh injury. Ethiopia's Dufera Darara Mokonen beat the third seed, Mohamed El-Beiali, to reach the semi-finals and win a home bronze.

events.name: Oceania Championships
story: Hwan Bae and Minhyung Jee won the singles at the Oceania Championships in Auckland. Bae, who was unseeded, beat the second seed, Finn Luu, 4-0 in the semi-finals and Aditya Sareen 4-1 in the final. Jee, the second seed, lost the first three games of the women's final to the top seed, Yangzi Liu, and won the next four, 14-12, 12-10, 11-3, 11-9.

Sareen had knocked out the top seed, Nicholas Lum, in the semi-finals. Lum still won two titles, the men's doubles with Luu and the mixed doubles with Liu, who also won the women's doubles with Jee. Australia's women beat New Zealand 3-0 in the team final.

events.name: WTT Champions Montpellier
story: Félix Lebrun and Satsuki Odo won WTT Champions Montpellier. Lebrun, the fourth seed, beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-1 in the final, 11-7, 11-9, 11-6, 8-11, 11-4, having beaten the top seed, Lin Shidong, 4-0 in the semi-finals. Odo, who was unseeded, beat Miwa Harimoto 4-2.

The top two women's seeds went out in the last 16, Wang Yidi to Qian Tianyi and Chen Xingtong to Egypt's Hana Goda, and Benedikt Duda beat Liang Jingkun 3-0 in the men's quarter-finals. Lebrun beat his brother Alexis in the quarter-finals, and Odo came from 3-2 down in games to beat Cheng I-Ching in the semi-finals.

events.name: WTT Champions Frankfurt
story: Lin Shidong and Wang Manyu won WTT Champions Frankfurt. Lin, the second seed, beat Anton Källberg 4-1 in the final, 11-5, 11-7, 11-9, 8-11, 11-8. Wang, the top seed, beat Wang Yidi 4-2.

Källberg, who was unseeded, beat the top seed, Wang Chuqin, 3-0 in the last 16 and his teammate Truls Moregard 4-2 in the semi-finals. Moregard had knocked out Félix Lebrun, and Lin Yun-Ju beat Hugo Calderano before losing 4-0 to Lin Shidong.

events.name: WTT Finals Fukuoka
story: Wang Chuqin and Wang Manyu won the WTT Finals in Kitakyushu. Wang Chuqin, the top seed, beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-0 in the final, 11-2, 11-8, 11-7, 11-5. Wang Manyu beat Chen Xingtong 4-3, winning the last two games after trailing 3-2.

Chen had knocked out the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 3-2 in the first round, and Harimoto beat Lin Shidong 4-3 in the semi-finals, taking the seventh game 12-10. Bernadette Szőcs beat Hina Hayata and Satsuki Odo, then came from 3-0 down to force a seventh game against Wang Manyu in the semi-finals, which Wang won 11-4. Félix and Alexis Lebrun won the men's doubles, and Honoka Hashimoto and Hitomi Sato the women's.

events.name: Pan American Championships
story: Hugo Calderano and Adriana Diaz, the top seeds, won the singles titles in Lima. Calderano beat Canada's Eugene Wang 4-2 in the men's final. Diaz beat Brazil's Bruna Takahashi 4-3 in the women's, 11-7 in the seventh game.

Wang was unseeded and had beaten the second seed, Gustavo Tsuboi, 4-0 in the last 16. Brazil won both team titles, the men beating Chile 3-1 and the women beating Canada 3-1, and Takahashi and Vitor Ishiy won the mixed doubles. Adriana and Melanie Diaz won the women's doubles for Puerto Rico, and Argentina's Horacio Cifuentes and Gaston Alto won the men's.

events.name: World Championships
story: Fan Zhendong and Wang Manyu won the singles titles in Houston. Fan, the top seed, beat Sweden's Truls Moregard 4-0 in the men's final, 11-6, 11-9, 11-7, 11-8. Wang, seeded fourth, came from two games down to beat the top seed, Chen Meng, 4-3 in the semi-finals and then beat Sun Yingsha 4-2, taking the sixth game 17-15.

Moregard was unseeded and beat Timo Boll 4-3 in the semi-finals. The men's draw had opened up early: Poland's Jakub Dyjas beat the second seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, in the last 64, and Lim Jonghoon beat the fourth seed, Lin Yun-Ju. Sweden's Kristian Karlsson and Mattias Falck won the men's doubles, and Sun took two titles, the women's doubles with Wang Manyu and the mixed with Wang Chuqin.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Doha
story: The top seeds, Tomokazu Harimoto and Mima Ito, won both singles titles for Japan. Harimoto beat Germany's Ruwen Filus 4-2 in the men's final and Ito beat Singapore's Feng Tianwei 4-1 in the women's.

Filus was unseeded and beat the third seed, Lin Yun-Ju, 3-0 in the quarter-finals, after Darko Jorgic had knocked out the second seed, Hugo Calderano. The second, third and fourth seeds in the women's draw all lost in the last 16. South Korea's Jeon Jihee and Shin Yubin beat the top seeds, Kasumi Ishikawa and Miu Hirano, 3-0 in the women's doubles final.

events.name: African Championships
story: Egypt won six of the seven titles in Yaoundé. Omar Assar beat Nigeria's Quadri Aruna 4-1 in the men's singles final, and Mariam Alhodaby came from 3-1 down to beat her teammate Hana Goda 4-3 in the women's. Egypt beat Nigeria in both team finals, 3-2 in the men's and 3-0 in the women's.

Assar also won the mixed doubles with Dina Meshref, and Farah Abdel-Aziz and Yousra Helmy won the women's doubles 4-3 against Nigeria's Cecilia Akpan and Offiong Edem. Nigeria's one title came in the men's doubles, where Aruna and Bode Abiodun beat Ahmed Saleh and Khalid Assar 4-2.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Doha
story: Hugo Calderano and Hina Hayata won the singles titles. Calderano, the second seed, beat Slovenia's Darko Jorgic 4-2 in the men's final. Hayata, seeded sixth, lost the first three games of her semi-final against the top seed, Jeon Jihee, won it 4-3, and then beat Hong Kong's Doo Hoi Kem 4-1 in the final.

Hayata also won the mixed doubles with Shunsuke Togami. The men's top seed, Dimitrij Ovtcharov, lost in the last 32 to South Korea's Cho Seungmin, who went on to win the men's doubles with An Jaehyun against England's Paul Drinkhall and Liam Pitchford.

events.name: WTT Cup Finals Singapore
story: Fan Zhendong and Sun Yingsha won the season-ending Cup Finals in Singapore. Fan, the top seed, beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-1 in the men's final, and Sun, seeded second, beat Wang Yidi 4-2 in the women's.

Wang had beaten the top seed, Chen Meng, 4-3 in the semi-finals, 12-10 in the seventh game. Harimoto beat the second seed, Hugo Calderano, 4-1 to reach the men's final, and Hong Kong's Doo Hoi Kem beat the third seed, Wang Manyu, 3-0 in the first round.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Doha
story: Two unseeded players won the singles titles, both from behind. Croatia's Andrej Gacina lost the first two games of the men's final to South Korea's Lim Jonghoon and won 4-2. Japan's Miyuu Kihara trailed Germany's Han Ying 3-1 in the women's final and won the last three games 11-7, 11-3, 11-1.

Kihara had beaten the second seed, Adriana Diaz, 3-0 in the last 32, and she also won the women's doubles with Miyu Nagasaki. Gacina won two of his first three matches 3-2, one of them against Truls Moregard. Germany's Dang Qiu and Benedikt Duda won the men's doubles, and France's Jia Nan Yuan and Emmanuel Lebesson beat the top seeds, Cheng I-Ching and Lin Yun-Ju, 3-0 in the mixed.

events.name: World Team Championships
story: China won both titles at the World Team Championships in Chengdu. The men beat Germany 3-0 in the final and the women beat Japan 3-0.

The men were taken closest in the semi-finals, where they beat Japan 3-2. Germany reached the final with two 3-2 wins, over France in the quarter-finals and South Korea in the semi-finals. China's women won their quarter-final, semi-final and final without losing a match, and Japan beat Germany 3-0 in the other semi-final.

events.name: Singapore Smash
story: Fan Zhendong and Chen Meng won the singles titles at the Singapore Smash, and both finals went to a seventh game. Fan, the top seed, led Ma Long 2-0, fell 3-2 behind and won the last two games 11-8, 11-7. Chen, seeded second, beat Wang Manyu 4-3, after Wang had beaten the top seed, Sun Yingsha, by the same score in the semi-finals.

China won all five titles. Fan and Wang Chuqin took the men's doubles, Sun and Wang Manyu the women's, and Sun and Wang Chuqin the mixed. Two of the top four men's seeds lost in the first round, Tomokazu Harimoto to Kanak Jha of the United States and Hugo Calderano to Portugal's João Geraldo, and Japan's Yukiya Uda, unseeded, reached the semi-finals.

events.name: WTT Macao
story: Wang Chuqin and Wang Manyu won the singles titles at WTT Macao, an invitational event. Wang Chuqin, seeded sixth, beat Lin Gaoyuan 4-3 in the men's final, 11-9 in the seventh game, having beaten Ma Long in the quarter-finals. Wang Manyu beat Liu Shiwen 4-0 in the women's final.

Wang Manyu had come through a 4-3 semi-final against the top seed, Chen Meng, and Liu had beaten the second seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2. Liu and Xu Xin won the mixed doubles, beating Kuai Man and Fan Zhendong 3-0 in the final.

events.name: WTT Star Contender European Summer Series
story: Wang Chuqin won the men's singles in Budapest without being seeded. He beat the third seed, Hugo Calderano, 3-2 in the last 16 and the top seed, Ma Long, 4-3 in the semi-finals, and then beat Sweden's Truls Moregard 4-1 in the final. Wang Yidi, the fourth seed, beat Sun Yingsha 4-1 in the women's final.

Wang Chuqin also won the mixed doubles with Wang Manyu, coming from two games down to beat Tomokazu Harimoto and Hina Hayata 3-2. Sun and Wang Manyu won the women's doubles, and South Korea's Cho Daeseong and Lee Sangsu beat Liang Jingkun and Lin Gaoyuan 3-2 in the men's.

events.name: WTT Champions European Summer Series
story: Tomokazu Harimoto lost the first three games of the men's final in Budapest and won it. The sixth seed beat China's Lin Gaoyuan 4-3, taking the last four games 11-6, 11-6, 13-11, 11-9. Wang Manyu, the third seed, beat Wang Yidi 4-2 in the women's final.

Three of the top four men's seeds were out by the end of the last 16: Patrick Franziska beat the top seed, Ma Long, Lim Jonghoon beat Hugo Calderano, and Marcos Freitas beat Truls Moregard. Both women's semi-finals went to seven games, with Wang Manyu coming from two games down to beat the top seed, Chen Meng, and Wang Yidi beating Sun Yingsha.

events.name: African Championships
story: Quadri Aruna won the men's singles in Algiers from 3-1 down, beating Egypt's Omar Assar 4-3 and taking the last two games 13-11 and 14-12. It reversed the result of the 2021 final. Dina Meshref beat her teammate Yousra Helmy 4-0 in the women's final.

Aruna's was the only title Egypt did not win. They beat Algeria 3-1 in the men's team final and Tunisia 3-0 in the women's, and all three doubles finals were between Egyptian pairs. Hana Goda won two of them, the women's doubles with Alaa Yehia and the mixed with Mohamed El-Beiali.

events.name: Pan American Championships
story: Hugo Calderano and Adriana Diaz kept their titles in Santiago. Calderano beat Kanak Jha of the United States 4-0 in the men's final. Diaz won her quarter-final and semi-final 4-3, against Amy Wang and Mo Zhang, and then beat Lily Zhang 4-1 in the final.

Brazil beat the United States 3-2 in both team finals, and Bruna Takahashi and Vitor Ishiy won the mixed doubles for the second year running. Amy Wang and Rachel Sung won the women's doubles for the United States, and Argentina's Horacio Cifuentes and Gaston Alto retained the men's.

events.name: Oceania Championships
story: Australia won every title in Melbourne, and all five individual finals were between Australian players. Nicholas Lum beat Xin Yan 4-1 in the men's singles final and Yangzi Liu beat Minhyung Jee 4-3 in the women's.
Lum won three titles, adding the men's doubles with Finn Luu and the mixed doubles with Jee. Liu won the women's doubles with Chunyi Feng.

events.name: WTT Champions Macao
story: Wang Chuqin won WTT Champions Macao without being seeded, beating the top seed, Fan Zhendong, 4-3 in the final. He had beaten Hugo Calderano, Dimitrij Ovtcharov, Ma Long and Truls Moregard to get there. Sun Yingsha, the women's top seed, beat Chen Xingtong 4-1 in her final.

Two of the top three women's seeds went out early. France's Jia Nan Yuan beat Wang Manyu 3-2 in the first round and went on to the semi-finals, and Bernadette Szőcs beat Chen Meng 3-2 in the last 16. In the men's draw Mattias Falck beat the fourth seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, and Alexis Lebrun beat the third, Liang Jingkun.

events.name: WTT Cup Finals Xinxiang
story: Wang Chuqin won the Cup Finals in Xinxiang a week after winning WTT Champions Macao. The sixth seed beat Tomokazu Harimoto 4-2 in the final, having led Ma Long 3-0 in the semi-finals, been pulled back to 3-3 and won the seventh game 11-8.
Sun Yingsha, the top seed, beat Chen Meng 4-3 in the women's final, 12-10 in the seventh game. It was her second title in two weeks as well.

events.name: Singapore Smash
story: Fan Zhendong beat Ma Long in the Singapore Smash final for the second year running, this time 4-1, and Sun Yingsha won three titles. Sun, the top seed, beat the unseeded Qian Tianyi 4-1 in the women's singles final and won the women's doubles with Wang Manyu and the mixed with Wang Chuqin.

China won all five events, with Fan and Wang Chuqin taking the men's doubles. Sun's closest match was her quarter-final, which she won 4-3 against South Korea's Joo Cheonhui. Two of the top four women's seeds lost in the last 32, Chen Meng to Elizabeta Samara and Wang Yidi to Miu Hirano, and Quadri Aruna beat the fourth seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, 3-0 in the men's last 16.

events.name: World Championships
story: Fan Zhendong retained the men's singles title in Durban and Sun Yingsha won the women's. Fan, the top seed, beat Wang Chuqin 4-2 in the final, and Sun, also seeded first, beat Chen Meng 4-2.

China won all five titles and all four men's semi-finalists were Chinese. Wang Chuqin reached three finals and won two of them, the men's doubles with Fan and the mixed with Sun. Chen Meng and Wang Yidi won the women's doubles against South Korea's Jeon Jihee and Shin Yubin.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Ljubljana
story: Both singles finals in Ljubljana were between China's top two seeds and both went to a seventh game. Fan Zhendong beat Wang Chuqin 4-3, 12-10 in the decider, and Sun Yingsha lost the first two games to Chen Meng before winning 4-3.

China won all five titles. Sun and Wang Chuqin took the mixed doubles, Wang Yidi and Kuai Man the women's, and Xiang Peng and Lin Shidong the men's, 3-2 against Ma Long and Yuan Licen. Zhou Qihao, unseeded, beat Ma 3-2 in the last 16 of the singles and reached the semi-finals.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Bangkok
story: Lin Gaoyuan and Chen Xingtong each won three titles in Bangkok. Lin, the third seed, beat South Korea's Jang Woojin 4-3 in the men's singles final, 11-9 in the seventh game. Chen, the women's top seed, beat South Korea's Joo Cheonhui 4-1.

They won the mixed doubles together, coming from two games down to beat Lim Jonghoon and Shin Yubin 3-2. Lin won the men's doubles with Lin Shidong and Chen the women's with Kuai Man. The top two men's seeds lost early, Tomokazu Harimoto to Xu Yingbin in the last 32 and Liang Jingkun to Anton Källberg in the last 16.

events.name: WTT Star Contender Goa
story: Liang Jingkun and Wang Yidi won the singles titles in Goa. Liang, the fourth seed, beat the unseeded Lin Shidong 4-2 in the men's final. Wang, the women's top seed, beat Cheng I-Ching 4-0.

The men's top seed, Fan Zhendong, lost 3-2 to South Korea's Cho Daeseong in the last 32. Félix Lebrun beat the third seed, Truls Moregard, and reached the semi-finals, and Miwa Harimoto beat the third seed, Kasumi Ishikawa, reached the women's semi-finals and won the women's doubles with Miyu Nagasaki. Cheng had knocked out the second seed, Hina Hayata.

events.name: WTT Champions Frankfurt
story: Lin Yun-Ju won WTT Champions Frankfurt as the eighth seed, beating Ma Long 4-1 in the final after a 4-2 win over the second seed, Wang Chuqin, in the semi-finals. Wang Yidi won the women's title, beating the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-2 in the semi-finals and Wang Manyu 4-0 in the final.

Two of the leading seeds had gone out in the last 16. South Korea's Lee Sangsu beat the men's top seed, Fan Zhendong, 3-1, and Bernadette Szőcs beat the women's second seed, Chen Meng, 3-2. Félix Lebrun reached the men's semi-finals, where he lost to Ma.

events.name: WTT Champions Macao
story: Wang Chuqin and Wang Manyu, both seeded second, won WTT Champions Macao. Wang Chuqin beat Ma Long 4-0 in the men's final, 12-10, 11-1, 11-8, 11-7, after a 3-2 quarter-final against Jang Woojin. Wang Manyu beat Chen Meng 4-2 in the women's final.
Chen had beaten the top seed, Sun Yingsha, 4-0 in the semi-finals. France's Alexis Lebrun, unseeded, reached the men's semi-finals, where he lost 4-1 to Ma.

events.name: WTT Feeder Vila Nova de Gaia
WTT Champions Xinxiang
story: The top seeds, Fan Zhendong and Sun Yingsha, won WTT Champions Xinxiang. Fan beat Liang Jingkun 4-1 in the men's final and Sun beat Wang Yidi 4-1 in the women's.

Fan came close to going out twice. He beat Lin Shidong 3-2 in the quarter-finals and South Korea's Lim Jonghoon 4-3 in the semi-finals, 11-9 in the seventh game. Lim had beaten the third seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, and Lin Yun-Ju had beaten the fourth, Ma Long, in the last 16.

events.name: WTT Finals Women Nagoya
story: Sun Yingsha won both titles at the women's WTT Finals in Nagoya. The top seed beat Wang Yidi 4-2 in the singles final and won the doubles with Wang Manyu, 3-1 against Japan's Miyuu Kihara and Miyu Nagasaki.
Her closest match was her first, a 3-2 win over Miwa Harimoto. She then beat Han Ying 3-0 and Chen Meng 4-1 to reach the final.

events.name: WTT Finals Men Doha
story: Wang Chuqin won the men's WTT Finals, played in Doha in January 2024 to close the 2023 season. The second seed beat the top seed, Fan Zhendong, 4-0 in the final, 11-8, 11-9, 14-12, 11-7.
Wang did not lose a game after the first round, beating Tomokazu Harimoto 3-0 and Dang Qiu 4-0. Xiang Peng and Yuan Licen, seeded seventh, won the doubles, 3-0 against Lin Gaoyuan and Lin Shidong.

events.name: WTT Feeder Vila Nova de Gaia
Mixed Team World Cup
story: China retained the Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu, beating South Korea 8-1 in the final. Ties are played to eight games, and China had won their semi-final against Romania by the same score.
South Korea reached the final by beating Hong Kong 8-5. Hong Kong took the bronze medal.

events.name: WTT Feeder Vila Nova de Gaia
Mixed Team World Cup
story: China won the Mixed Team World Cup for the third year in a row, beating Japan 8-1 in the final in Chengdu.
China beat South Korea 8-3 in the semi-finals and Japan beat Germany by the same score. Germany took the bronze medal.

events.name: WTT Feeder Vila Nova de Gaia
African Championships
story: Quadri Aruna and Hana Goda won the singles titles in Tunis. Aruna, the top seed, beat Egypt's Ahmed Saleh 4-0 in the men's final, and Goda beat the top seed, Dina Meshref, 4-1 in the women's.

Egypt beat Nigeria in both team finals, 3-1 in the men's and 3-0 in the women's. Congo's Saheed Idowu knocked out the men's second seed, Omar Assar, 4-0 in the quarter-finals, and Madagascar's Fabio Rakotoarimanana and Antoine Razafinarivo won the men's doubles. Assar and Meshref won the mixed doubles, as they had in 2021.

events.name: Pan American Championships
story: Hugo Calderano won the men's singles in Havana for the third year in a row, beating Chile's Nicolas Burgos 4-1 in the final. Amy Wang of the United States won the women's title, 4-3 against Bruna Takahashi and 12-10 in the seventh game.

Wang had come from 3-1 down to beat Adriana Diaz, the champion of the two previous years, 4-3 in the semi-finals. Burgos won two doubles titles for Chile, the men's with Gustavo Gomez and the mixed with Paulina Vega, and Adriana and Melanie Diaz won the women's doubles.

events.name: Olympic Games
story: China won four of the five gold medals at the Tokyo Games, which were held a year late, in 2021. Ma Long beat Fan Zhendong 4-2 in the men's singles final, 11-4, 10-12, 11-8, 11-9, 3-11, 11-7, and Chen Meng beat Sun Yingsha 4-2 in the women's. China beat Germany 3-0 in the men's team final and Japan 3-0 in the women's.

The exception was the mixed doubles, where Japan's Jun Mizutani and Mima Ito lost the first two games of the final to Xu Xin and Liu Shiwen and won 4-3. Both men's singles semi-finals went to seven games: Fan beat Lin Yun-Ju and Ma beat Dimitrij Ovtcharov, who took the bronze medal. Slovenia's Darko Jorgic knocked out the third seed, Tomokazu Harimoto, in the last 16, and Singapore's Yu Mengyu, unseeded, reached the women's semi-finals.

events.name: European Championships
story: Germany won four of the five titles at the European Championships in Warsaw, which were due to be played in September 2020 and were put back to June 2021 by the pandemic. Both singles finals were all-German: Timo Boll beat Dimitrij Ovtcharov for the men's title and Petrissa Solja beat Shan Xiaona for the women's.

Solja and Shan then won the women's doubles together, beating their teammates Nina Mittelham and Sabine Winter, and Mittelham won the mixed doubles with Dang Qiu. The one title Germany did not win was the men's doubles, which went to Russia's Lev Katsman and Maksim Grebnev.

events.name: European Team Championships
story: Germany won both titles at the European Team Championships in Cluj-Napoca. The men beat Russia in their final and the women beat the hosts, Romania.
It completed a year in which Germany also won four of the five titles at the individual European Championships in Warsaw.

events.name: Asian Championships

runner_up.name: Doo Hoi Kem / Lee Ho Ching

story: China did not send a team to the Asian Championships in Doha, and Japan and South Korea shared the titles. Japan won four: Hina Hayata took the women's singles, the mixed doubles with Shunsuke Togami and the women's team title, and Togami and Yukiya Uda won the men's doubles.

South Korea won the other three. Lee Sangsu beat Chinese Taipei's Chuang Chih-Yuan in the men's singles final, Jeon Jihee and Shin Yubin won the women's doubles, and the men beat Chinese Taipei in the team final. Shin, who also reached the women's singles final, finished with a medal in three events.

events.name: European Championships
story: Dang Qiu won the men's singles at home in Munich, beating Slovenia's Darko Jorgic in the final, and Austria's Sofia Polcanova won two titles. Polcanova beat Germany's Nina Mittelham in the women's singles final and won the women's doubles with Romania's Bernadette Szőcs.

Sweden's Mattias Falck and Kristian Karlsson won the men's doubles against Austria's Robert Gardos and Daniel Habesohn. Szőcs also reached the mixed doubles final with Ovidiu Ionescu, where they lost to France's Emmanuel Lebesson and Jia Nan Yuan.

events.name: European Games
story: Félix Lebrun won the men's singles at the European Games in Kraków, beating Portugal's Marcos Freitas in the final. Bernadette Szőcs won two gold medals for Romania: the women's singles, against Monaco's Yang Xiaoxin, and the women's team event, where Romania beat Germany in the final.

Germany won the other two titles. Dang Qiu and Nina Mittelham took the mixed doubles against Hungary's Nándor Ecseki and Dóra Madarász, and the men's team of Timo Boll, Patrick Franziska, Dimitrij Ovtcharov and Dang beat Sweden for gold.

events.name: European Team Championships
story: Sweden won the men's title at home in Malmö, beating Germany in the final with a squad of Mattias Falck, Anton Källberg, Kristian Karlsson, Truls Moregard and Jon Persson. Germany's women beat Romania in their final.

Both winners earned a place in the team events at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. Germany's men were runners-up with a squad of Timo Boll, Benedikt Duda, Cedric Meissner, Kay Stumper and Ricardo Walther, and Romania's women lost to Germany in the final for the second championships in a row.

events.name: Asian Championships
story: China won all seven titles at the Asian Championships in Pyeongchang, and all five individual finals were between Chinese players. Ma Long beat Fan Zhendong in the men's singles final and Wang Manyu beat Sun Yingsha in the women's.

Wang Manyu also won the women's doubles with Chen Meng. Fan and Lin Gaoyuan beat Ma and Wang Chuqin in the men's doubles final, and Lin won the mixed doubles with Wang Yidi. China's men beat Chinese Taipei in the team final and the women beat the hosts, South Korea.

events.name: Asian Games

runner_up.name: Cha Su Yong / Pak Su Gyong

story: Wang Chuqin won four gold medals at the Asian Games in Hangzhou, which were held a year late, in 2023. He beat Fan Zhendong in the men's singles final, won the men's doubles with Fan and the mixed doubles with Sun Yingsha, and was part of the China team that beat South Korea. Sun won the women's singles against Japan's Hina Hayata and the women's team title.
China won six of the seven events. The exception was the women's doubles, in which South Korea's Jeon Jihee and Shin Yubin beat North Korea's Cha Su Yong and Pak Su Gyong in the final.

events.name: Mixed Team World Cup

champions.note: Won the final stage, which was played as a round robin. South Korea were second and Japan third

story: China won the first Mixed Team World Cup, in Chengdu. There was no final: the title was decided by a round-robin second stage, which China won, with South Korea taking silver and Japan bronze.

The event used a new format in which men and women play in the same team. A tie is made up of a mixed doubles, a women's singles, a men's singles and women's and men's doubles, each played over three games, and the first team to win eight games takes the tie.

events.name: Oceania Championships
story: Australia won every senior title in Townsville. Aditya Sareen beat Finn Luu in the men's singles final and Yangzi Liu beat Minhyung Jee in the women's, her second title in a row, and the two of them won the mixed doubles together.

Sareen was young enough to play in Australia's under-15 team at the same championships, which were held alongside the youth events, and he also won the under-19 boys' singles. Nicholas Lum, the 2022 men's champion, won the men's doubles with Luu for the second year running, and Jee and Jian Fang Lay won the women's doubles.
